title: Build a Lead Research Agent Without Buying a Full Sales Stack
summary: Build a lead research agent with observable fit rules, company evidence, selective enrichment, deduplication, and a human-reviewable shortlist.
body_markdown:
A lead research agent should help a person decide which companies deserve attention and why. It needs evidence of fit, a reliable company identity, and a concise explanation of the potential use case. A spreadsheet full of names and guessed email addresses is a different outcome.


You can prototype the research portion without buying an entire sales platform. Start with web discovery, company-page retrieval, and selective enrichment through a shared tool interface. This article describes a reference design rather than a live campaign. It does not authorize outreach, assume access to private profiles, or claim that every discussed provider is currently wallet-funded through o11.


## Turn the customer profile into observable rules


An ideal customer profile is useful to an agent only when it can test it. “Innovative businesses that need AI” is too broad. “Self-serve software companies offering a public API and a free trial, with documentation that describes asynchronous jobs” gives the agent observable signals.


Separate must-have rules from preferences. A public API could be required. A particular funding stage might be a preference if reliable evidence is difficult to obtain. Exclusion rules deserve equal attention: unsupported geography, a service-only business model, an existing customer, or a prior opt-out should prevent inappropriate selection.


For each rule, define acceptable evidence and an unknown state. The absence of a visible free-trial button does not establish that a trial is unavailable. Mark it unknown unless the site’s terms or pricing page establish the answer. This prevents the model from treating a sparse website as a complete description of the business.


## Research companies before people


Resolve the company name and domain, then verify the product and buying context. A useful first record contains the canonical domain, product description, customer segment, evidence URLs, and a short reason for inclusion. Only research a person when the task requires a specific role and you have a legitimate, authorized source.


[Exa documents people-oriented search](https://exa.ai/library/person) , while[People Data Labs documents company enrichment](https://docs.peopledatalabs.com/docs/company-enrichment-api) . Those are examples of different research capabilities. They do not remove the need to check identity, source quality, appropriate use, or the account-specific rights attached to the returned data.


Company-first research keeps the experiment focused. If a business is outside the target profile, there is little value in buying multiple person-level records. If the company matches, the researcher can decide whether a role lookup is necessary or whether the public contact path is sufficient for a later, separately authorized action.


## Build an evidence-backed shortlist


Use a narrow output schema rather than a free-form research essay. The fields should support the decision a human will make:


Field What belongs there


Company identity Canonical name and domain


Fit signals Specific observed facts tied to the target rules


Relevant use case A clearly labeled interpretation of those facts


Evidence URLs, passages, and observation dates


Uncertainty Missing or conflicting information


Disposition Review, defer, exclude, or already covered


Avoid precision that the evidence cannot support. A score of 87.4 does not make weak source material more reliable. A categorical assessment with explicit reasons is often easier to review. If you use a numeric score, publish the rubric internally and keep the underlying signals so a person can challenge it.


Use[JSON Schema’s object rules](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/object) to distinguish required fields from optional observations. The schema catches missing structure; factual review still needs source checks.


## Choose the smallest useful tool stack


Start with one discovery operation and one page-reading operation. Add company enrichment only when it resolves a recurring gap. Add role research only after company fit is established. This is usually a more informative prototype than connecting a dozen services before reviewing the first result.


A shared interface can reduce the number of client integrations the developer writes. It does not make supplier data interchangeable. Different sources use different company definitions, update schedules, identifiers, and coverage. Preserve provider provenance and avoid silently replacing one field with another because both are called employee count.


In o11, verify the exact operation, input contract, selected account, and quote before execution. A customer-account operation may require a connected provider account. An available catalog description does not prove live execution under your workspace.[The provider-account guide](https://o11.ai/blog/provider-accounts-and-pay-per-use-tools) explains the access choices.


Keep outreach tools outside this research agent’s scope. Researching a potential fit should not automatically send a message, update a shared CRM, or subscribe someone to a sequence. Those actions need their own explicit workflow and authorization.


## Spend only when the next call can change the decision


Before each extra lookup, ask which decision it can alter. An enrichment call that might resolve a required geography is useful. A fifth company description that repeats the homepage rarely is. This is a practical stopping rule for both cost and research quality.


Consider an illustrative batch of 40 companies. Assume first-pass research costs $0.04 per company, 12 candidates require a $0.10 enrichment call, and six require another $0.03 retrieval. Tool cost is $1.60 + $1.20 + $0.18 = $2.98. If nine companies pass review, the tool cost per accepted company is approximately $0.33. These inputs are hypothetical, exclude inference and labor, and are not provider pricing.


This staged calculation tells you where to improve. If most companies fail a simple rule, refine discovery before adding richer data. If reviewers reject ostensibly qualified companies, strengthen the evidence rubric. Buying more data cannot rescue an unclear definition of fit.


Track the same denominator across tool stacks.[Comparing research workflow costs](https://o11.ai/blog/compare-research-workflow-costs) covers why accepted outputs are a better unit than API calls.


## Deduplicate before and after enrichment


Normalize domains and keep aliases for brands, legal entities, and redirects. A company may have a marketing site, an application domain, and a separate documentation domain. A naive domain comparison can treat those as three prospects. A name comparison can merge unrelated businesses.


Use a stable internal company record and link source identifiers to it. Keep ambiguous candidates separate until the evidence supports a merge. Record the reason for the merge so future corrections do not require redoing the whole batch.


Before exporting a shortlist, check it against the team’s existing records and exclusions through an authorized, read-only interface. Preserve opt-outs and duplicate-contact protections if a later outreach workflow uses the results. A new research run should not erase a prior decision merely because its source data is fresher.


Handle concurrency at the record level. Two researchers discovering the same company should converge on one reviewable item, with both source trails retained. This is particularly valuable when several agents explore adjacent segments at once.


## Make failures reviewable and local


If one website blocks extraction, preserve its identity and mark the unresolved criteria. Continue with the other companies. If a source returns a stale title, retain the conflict instead of confidently naming a current buyer. If a provider is unavailable, defer the affected lookup with a retry time or a manual path.


Separate provider failure from research failure. A successful response with irrelevant data may be less useful than a transparent timeout. Log both operational status and whether the result changed the qualification decision. Do not call an enriched record “verified” merely because the provider returned HTTP success.


When a paid request has an uncertain outcome, inspect its existing status before trying again. This matters for batch work, where an automatic restart can quietly duplicate many purchases.[The recovery guide](https://o11.ai/blog/agent-tool-failures-recovery) explains how to classify retryable and uncertain cases.


## Evaluate the shortlist before scaling it


Start with a small, diverse sample and have a knowledgeable teammate review the evidence. Record whether each company truly matches, whether the use-case explanation is grounded, and which critical questions remain. Review a few excluded companies too; otherwise you will measure only false positives and miss good candidates the agent rejected.


Track accepted companies per reviewed batch, evidence completeness, duplicate rate, manual correction time, and cost per accepted company. These measurements help determine whether another paid source saves useful work. They are also a better basis for choosing a subscription than the total number of available records.


Expand only after the review process is predictable. The point of a lightweight tool stack is to learn what your team actually needs before committing to an extensive sales system. A good research agent makes the shortlist easier to trust and the next human decision easier to make.


## Example: a shortlist entry a person can check


For a fictional API startup, an entry might say: “Review. Public documentation describes a self-serve API and a usage-based plan. The product page targets engineering teams. The current geography requirement is unresolved.” Each observed signal should link to its supporting page. The suggested use case belongs in a separate interpretation field.


That entry is more useful than “Excellent fit, 95% confidence.” A reviewer can confirm the relevant facts and decide whether the unknown geography warrants another lookup. If geography is mandatory, the disposition stays deferred until evidence resolves it. If it is only a preference, the company may remain reviewable with the limitation visible.


Use the same format for exclusions. “Excluded because the official site describes a consulting-only offer” gives the team a reason it can revisit if the business changes. “Bad lead” does not preserve useful context.


When reviewing the prototype, sample both groups. Check whether the agent overuses unknown, mistakes a reseller for a product company, or interprets a free consultation as a free trial. These are concrete qualification errors that better discovery and source reading can address before the team buys additional data.
